newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain repeats call for wage moderation.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain repeats call for wage moderation.

text.p: Spanish wage rises should continue to moderate so that companies' financial health can improve and inflation can continue converging with the rest of Europe, Bank of Spain research director Jose Luis Malo de Molina said on Friday.

Personnel costs at Spanish firms rose on average 4.7 percent in the first nine months of the year. But this rate "is not consistent with the necessary deflation of the economy and with the inflation convergence trend," Malo de Molina said. He was speaking at the presentation of the central bank's quarterly report on the non-financial business sector.
Firms have gradually become healthier because of lower financial charges amid cuts in lending rates, as well as lower depreciation, the Bank of Spain said.
But future improvement should stem from operating margin growth, Malo de Molina said.
